subject: Request: elevated availability commitment for Phoenix Health (prod)
body:
--- Message 1 (initial request) ---
From: Alice Foster <alice.foster@phoenixhealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, procurement@phoenixhealth.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: SLA request for Phoenix production rollout

Rishi —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Phoenix is planning to cut over our clinical inference pipeline to Redwood next quarter. Security and procurement teams have asked us to get an explicit availability and latency commitment for the prod workload before final approval.

Specifically they're requesting:
- 99.98% monthly uptime for inference endpoints in us-west-2 (business hours and 24/7 for critical flows)
- P99 latency < 220ms for text-generation requests with avg prompt length ~600 tokens
- A credit/penalty schedule for missed commitments (they prefer simple financial credits)

I've attached our traffic snapshot and a short procurement memo. Happy to jump on a call to clarify. Procurement (procurement@phoenixhealth.com) is on copy so you have the right contacts.

Best,
Alice Foster
Head of Platform Integrations
Phoenix Health

Attachments: phoenix-sla-request.pdf, phoenix-traffic-report.csv

--- Message 2 (acknowledgement & internal loop-in) ---
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alice Foster <alice.foster@phoenixhealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLA request for Phoenix production rollout

Alice —

Thanks for the details and the attachments. We appreciate the heads-up on the procurement asks. Monica will be our CS lead on this; Marissa and I will coordinate commercial terms. I've looped in Maya (Product) to validate feasibility on latency numbers and any product-side roadmap asks that might affect a commitment.

Quick questions to help us evaluate:
1) Is the 99.98% monthly uptime a hard cutover requirement or a target for the first 3 months?
2) For the P99 latency target, can you confirm the distribution of request sizes (we saw a ~600 token avg but want percentiles for <=300 / 300-800 / >800)?
3) Do you anticipate traffic spikes (traffic report shows a small daily burst around 01:00 UTC) that should be treated as critical?

We'll come back with a recommended approach (carved SLA, fallback model variants, credit schedule). Can we book a 30m sync Thursday if that works for your procurement team?

Thanks —
Rishi
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference

--- Message 3 (internal product/eng assessment) ---
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLA request for Phoenix production rollout

Team —

I reviewed the traffic dump and Phoenix's ask. Quick notes:
- 99.98% monthly (≈8.6 minutes downtime/month) is above our standard hosted commitment (we normally publish 99.9% for standard plans; Dedicated reserved capacity can target higher SLOs).
- P99 <220ms for ~600 token prompts on us-west-2 GPUs is aggressive for shared-hosted tiers during peak times unless we reserve capacity or use Dedicated pools + KV cache priming.

Possible mitigations:
- Offer a Dedicated pool with a 99.98% uptime SLA and a P99 latency target tied to a reserved throughput level (e.g., X qps sustained). This requires a committed capacity contract.
- If customer stays on Hosted, we can provide a staged commitment: 99.95% first quarter, with an operational runbook and automatic fallback to a smaller-latency-optimized model (with documented model-variant behavior).

Open questions for procurement negotiation:
- Do they have appetite for a committed spend (monthly GPU reservation)?
- Are they flexible on latency SLO if we bind it to a committed throughput bucket?

Aditya, can your team estimate what reserved GPU pool size we'd need for Phoenix's 95th traffic percentile to achieve the P99 <220ms target?

Thanks,
Maya
Product Lead, Serving Runtime

--- Message 4 (engineering estimate) ---
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 15:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLA request for Phoenix production rollout

Maya/Rishi —

We ran a quick capacity sim against the traffic snapshot. Short answer: to guarantee P99 <220ms at peak with 600 token avg we need a Dedicated pool sized at roughly 12 A100-equivalent slots (with continuous batching and prefix cache enabled), assuming traffic profile scales as in their CSV. If Phoenix can't commit to dedicated capacity we'll need to scope a lower P99 target or add burst routing to alternate regions.

Implications:
- Dedicated pool => commercial reserved contract (monthly commit), which materially changes pricing and adds procurement lead time (~4-6 weeks for provisioning and contractual review).
- We should include an SLA credit schedule tied to total monthly downtime minutes. For quick negotiation, I suggest: 10% service credit for downtime between 99.95% and 99.98%, 25% credit for <99.95%. Legal/commercial can refine wording.

I'll attach a proposed draft SLA for redlines.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Sr. Infra Engineer (Inference Runtime)

Attachment: proposed-sla-redwood-draft.docx

--- Message 5 (executive approval + reply to external) ---
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Alice Foster <alice.foster@phoenixhealth.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLA request for Phoenix production rollout

Alice / Phoenix team —

Appreciate the patience while we assessed feasibility. Redwood can support Phoenix's request with the following commercial/operational package: 

1) Dedicated capacity reservation sized to Phoenix's 95th percentile (estimated 12 A100-equivalent slots)
2) Commitment: 99.98% monthly uptime for the Dedicated-backed endpoints in us-west-2
3) Latency: P99 target of 220ms tied to the reserved throughput bucket; deviations during exceptional force majeure or sustained traffic exceeding committed throughput will be escalated but not considered SLA violations if we can show autoscaling constraints and cross-region fallbacks attempted
4) Credit schedule (draft): 10% monthly credit for uptime between 99.95% and 99.98%; 25% credit for uptime <99.95% (subject to standard exclusions)
5) Operational: onboarding runbook, weekly check-ins for first 90 days, and a cross-team tabletop for incident scenarios

Next steps for Phoenix: confirm willingness to commit to the dedicated contract and proposed provisioning lead time so we can issue a commitment addendum. Once Phoenix confirms, we'll route the draft SLA and DocuSign link to procurement.

Rishi/Marissa/Monica: please coordinate the commercial terms and send the addendum to procurement. Marissa — please prepare a high-level pricing estimate using the 12-slot baseline and include setup lead time.

Alice — happy to take a 30m call this week if you'd like to walk through the addendum before it goes to legal.

Best,
Laura Bennett
VP, Customer Success & Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced earlier: phoenix-sla-request.pdf, phoenix-traffic-report.csv, proposed-sla-redwood-draft.docx
DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/en/documents/PHX-SLA-EXCEPTION-2026

--- End of thread ---
